testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light is red. It may also make a buzzer sound. All vehicles with air brakes must have this warning light.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, what does it mean?

options.text: The ABS cannot work due to weather.
The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: When the ABS light comes on, it means there is a problem with the Anti-Lock Braking System.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: One air brake system with two sets of controls.
One air brake system for each side of the truck.
Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two completely separate air brake systems. They share one set of controls. One system controls the rear brakes, and the other controls the front brakes.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil are found in the compressed air of an air brake system. What should be done with them?

options.text: They are necessary for the system to work.
They should make up about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: Water and compressor oil can damage the air brake system if they build up. Air tanks have drains that should be opened at the end of each day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are installed on all four wheels of a vehicle. The s-cam drum brake is the most common type.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, must be equipped with anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: What are activated by an electric switch triggered by the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: When you push the brake pedal, air pressure triggers an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights to alert other drivers.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how much distance does brake lag add to stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Brake lag is the delay before the brakes start working. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how are the two systems separated?

options.text: Each system has separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks, but have separate hoses and lines.
Each system uses the same lines and hoses.
One is the main system and one is a backup if the first fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: Each system in a dual air brake system is completely separate with its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. Both systems share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: To let rain water into the tank.
To drain water and oil from the tank.
They must stay open while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: To drain water and oil from the tank.
questions.explanation: Water and oil buildup in the air tank can damage the brakes. Drain valves must be opened daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Using brakes creates heat. If too much heat builds up:

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes are made to handle a lot of heat. However, if brakes get too hot, they can fade and lose stopping power. Drivers should also use engine braking to slow the vehicle.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to:

options.text: Make the brakes work without squeaking.
Stop ice from forming in the brake system.
Keep people from breathing the air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: While driving, ____ normally holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator stops ice from building up in an air brake system. Check and refill it every day in cold weather.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: The parking brake is controlled by a knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: To check if a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for the ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle for the control unit and sensor wires on the back of the brakes.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: Front wheel brakes work:

options.text: Only if the road is dry.

questions.explanation: Front wheel brakes work in all road conditions. You are unlikely to have a front wheel skid, even on ice.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in an S-cam brake system, air pressure pushes out the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in an S-cam brake system, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build at least ____ psi in both systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than ____ of air pressure in one minute.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 5 psi of air pressure in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Air brakes work using ____.
questions.explanation: Air brakes use compressed air to work.

questions.question: Which one is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate braking systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens after air pressure is lost and the spring brakes engage?

options.text: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes.
You can continue driving normally using the spring brakes.
The air tanks automatically refill to a safe pressure level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can temporarily release the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank. If the spring brakes engage due to low air pressure, you can push a control to use this separate tank. This will temporarily release the spring brakes, allowing you to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: ____ make up the emergency brake system.

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three separate braking systems: a service brake system, a parking brake system, and an emergency brake system. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.
